You are the implementing engineer for Atlas ERP, in '/Users/taha/Claude projects/expremental ERP/atlas-erp' on branch feat/procurement-goods-receipt (based on the 6.2 procurement chain; core+finance+inventory+procurement-6.2 all present). NO git commands. uv at ~/.local/bin/uv; run `cd backend && ~/.local/bin/uv run <cmd>`. PostgreSQL 16 at postgresql+asyncpg://atlas:atlas@localhost:55432/atlas (LOCAL, available — run the full pg suite).

This is the procurement → inventory → finance integration: a goods receipt against a PO creates inventory stock RECEIPT moves whose valuation journal credits **GR/IR clearing** (not the standalone price-difference offset), via the existing 5.3 costing event. Read the costing/event design FULLY first.

READ FIRST (binding):
- docs/architecture.md **D-020** (inventory costing: a stock RECEIPT publishes StockValued and finance/handlers.py posts Dr Inventory / Cr offset; the offset for a STANDALONE receipt is price-difference, and the handler docstring explicitly says "procurement's goods-receipt path will OVERRIDE this with its own GR/IR offset" — you implement that override now), **D-011** (event bus, same-transaction), D-012/D-013/D-014 (numbered GR document, idempotency, pagination), D-029 (opaque ids), D-022/D-025 (migrations/tests), D-007 (tenancy).
- The EXACT code you integrate with:
  - backend/app/modules/inventory/service/stock_moves.py (create_move — learn its signature; you'll call it for each received line) + service/costing.py + events.py (StockValued — see how offset_account_id is currently chosen for a RECEIPT) + finance/handlers.py (post_stock_valuation_journal — how the offset becomes the Cr leg). You must add a way for the CALLER (the goods receipt) to OVERRIDE the receipt's valuation offset account to the GR/IR clearing account. Cleanest: add an optional `valuation_offset_account_id` param to create_move (default None → costing engine uses its standard offset per move type; when provided for a RECEIPT, the StockValued event carries it as offset_account_id so the handler credits GR/IR). Implement that override path end-to-end (create_move → costing publish → StockValued.offset_account_id → handler) WITHOUT breaking the existing standalone-receipt tests (default behavior unchanged).
  - backend/app/modules/finance/constants/documents.py (POSTING purposes — add a 'gr_ir_clearing' purpose) + finance/service/posting_defaults.py + finance/queries.py (add a query to fetch the GR/IR clearing account id for a tenant: get_posting_default_account(purpose) or similar following the existing posting-default lookup; if such a query already exists, reuse it). The GR/IR clearing account is a per-tenant posting default (a finance account, LIABILITY/clearing). 
  - backend/app/modules/procurement/ (6.2): models/ (PurchaseOrder/Line with received_quantity + status lifecycle PARTIALLY_RECEIVED/RECEIVED already declared), service/orders.py, queries.py (get_po_for_receipt, po_line_open_quantity), constants.py (statuses, sequences, doc/link types), router structure (sibling routers mounted into router.py).
  - backend/app/modules/inventory/queries.py (get_item, get_category_accounts — the receipt needs the item's inventory account; the costing engine already resolves inventory+price-diff from the category, you only override the offset).
  - backend/tests/modules/procurement/{factories.py, conftest.py} and backend/tests/modules/inventory/factories.py (warehouse/bin/item-with-GL-accounts/open-period wiring the costing handler needs) and a finance posting-default fixture.
Latest migration = 0025.

TASK — PLAN 6.3: goods receipt against a PO → stock move + GR/IR journal, docflow links, optional inspection hook. Build:

1. finance: add a 'gr_ir_clearing' posting purpose/default (constants/documents.py + wherever purposes are registered) and a finance/queries helper to fetch the GR/IR clearing account id for the current tenant (raise a clear error if the tenant hasn't configured one — a GR can't post without it). This is the account the GR credits and the 6.4 bill will debit. Document.
2. inventory: add the `valuation_offset_account_id` override to create_move + thread it through costing → StockValued → finance handler (as above). Add/extend tests proving: a RECEIPT WITHOUT override still credits price-difference (unchanged); a RECEIPT WITH the override credits the given account (GR/IR). Keep all existing inventory tests green.
3. procurement constants additions: GoodsReceiptStatus (DRAFT|POSTED|CANCELLED — a GR posts atomically like a stock move; or DRAFT then POST — choose POSTED-on-create-atomic OR a draft→post; mirror how stock moves work (posted at creation) but a GR is a document the user builds line-by-line then posts, so DRAFT→POSTED is better — decide and document); permissions procurement.goods_receipt.read/.manage/.post; number sequence 'procurement.goods_receipt' (GR-…); doc type + docflow link types PO→GR ("received_by") and GR→stock-move ("posts"/"moved_by"). An InspectionRequired flag source: the item or item-category carries whether received stock needs inspection — for v1 the "inspection hook" is just a per-line `requires_inspection` boolean (sourced from the item/category, or set on the GR line) and the received stock goes to a designated inspection/QI bin OR is flagged needs_inspection=true on the move/quant — KEEP IT A FLAG ONLY (the inspection lot lifecycle is Phase 9). Document precisely what the flag does in v1 (flag the GR line + optionally route to an inspection bin; no blocking of downstream use yet — Phase 9 adds the disposition).
4. procurement models (new models/goods_receipts.py, re-export in models/__init__.py): `GoodsReceipt` (`proc_goods_receipts`): DocumentMixin header; gr_number, status, purchase_order_id (composite tenant_fk to proc_purchase_orders), vendor_id (snapshot), warehouse_id (opaque inventory warehouse id — validated via inventory/queries; or composite? warehouse is in inventory, so OPAQUE id validated via inventory/queries per D-029), receipt_date, notes, posted_at. `GoodsReceiptLine` (`proc_goods_receipt_lines`): line_number, purchase_order_line_id (composite tenant_fk to proc_purchase_order_lines), item_id (opaque, snapshot from PO line), bin_id (opaque inventory bin id — where the stock lands, validated via inventory/queries), received_quantity (QuantityType), unit_cost (MoneyType — snapshot from PO line), lot_code/serial_code (nullable — for lot/serial-tracked items, passed to the stock move), requires_inspection (bool), stock_move_id (nullable composite — the move this line generated). UNIQUE(tenant_id, gr_id, line_number). 
5. procurement service (new service/goods_receipts.py, <400 lines — split reads into goods_receipt_reads.py if needed): 
   - create_goods_receipt(po_id, lines[(po_line_id, bin_id, qty, lot/serial, requires_inspection)], receipt_date) — DRAFT; validate the PO is APPROVED/SENT (can receive against), each po_line belongs to the PO, qty > 0 and qty <= open quantity (ordered - received) via procurement/queries.po_line_open_quantity (over-receipt policy: REJECT over-receipt beyond open qty in v1 → 422 procurement.over_receipt; document; tolerance is a later), bin exists in inventory, item matches the PO line's item. Claim GR number.
   - post_goods_receipt(gr_id) — the heart, in run_in_uow: for each line, call inventory.create_move(RECEIPT, item, qty, to_bin=bin, unit_cost=line.unit_cost, lot/serial, move_date=receipt_date, valuation_offset_account_id=GR/IR clearing account) → which posts Dr Inventory / Cr GR-IR via the costing event in the same transaction; store stock_move_id on the line; raise received_quantity on the PO line (+= qty) and advance PO status (PARTIALLY_RECEIVED if any open remains, RECEIVED if all lines fully received) via procurement orders service/queries; link docflow PO→GR and GR→each stock move; set GR status POSTED, posted_at. A closed-period receipt_date makes the move's journal trip the period trigger → whole post rolls back (document — correct). Idempotent (D-013); re-post of a POSTED GR rejected. The whole thing is ONE transaction: GR + N moves + N inventory-debit/GR-IR journals + PO status update.
   - cancel: DRAFT only (POSTED GR is corrected by a reversing GR or a return — note returns are a later/Phase 7 RMA concept; for v1 a POSTED GR cannot be cancelled, document; if you implement a reverse_goods_receipt that reverses the moves, that's a bonus but keep scope tight — prefer DRAFT-cancel-only + document POSTED is terminal).
   - Background-job the post above N lines? A GR is typically small (a delivery); keep it inline. Document no background path needed (unlike bulk runs).
6. procurement queries additions: get_goods_receipt, goods_receipts_for_po. 
7. procurement events: NOW the first procurement event MAY be relevant — but actually the GR posts to inventory by CALLING inventory.create_move directly (procurement → inventory/service is NOT allowed per STRUCTURE §5! Modules don't import each other's service). RE-READ STRUCTURE §5: "Modules never import each other's service.py or models.py directly. Cross-module effects go through the event bus." So procurement CANNOT call inventory.create_move directly. The goods receipt must publish an event that inventory handles, OR inventory exposes the move-creation through a sanctioned interface. 
   RESOLUTION: This is the crux. Options: (a) procurement publishes GoodsReceiptPosted; an inventory HANDLER (inventory/handlers.py — created now) receives it and creates the stock moves in the same transaction (run_in_uow), and the move's costing event in turn triggers finance's journal — a two-hop same-transaction chain. (b) inventory exposes a narrow command interface in inventory/queries.py or a new sanctioned module API. Per the architecture (D-011, events are the cross-module mechanism; queries.py is for READS only), the correct pattern is (a): procurement publishes a domain event, inventory subscribes and performs the stock move. VERIFY this against how the existing inventory→finance COGS works (inventory publishes StockValued, finance handles) — yes, same pattern. So: procurement/events.py defines GoodsReceiptPosted (carrying the lines: item, bin, qty, unit_cost, lot/serial, the GR/IR offset account, move_date, the GR document id for docflow); inventory/handlers.py subscribes and calls its OWN service.create_move per line (inventory calling its own service is fine), setting valuation_offset_account_id, and writes stock_move_id back... BUT the handler can't easily write back onto the procurement GR line (that's procurement's table). 
   Resolve the write-back: the procurement service, after publishing, can't know the move ids synchronously. Cleaner: the GR post publishes the event with the GR line ids; inventory's handler creates the moves and, because handlers share the session, can update the procurement GR lines' stock_move_id? No — inventory updating procurement tables violates ownership. 
   BEST RESOLUTION honoring §5: invert it — the goods-receipt service computes everything and emits ONE event per line OR the handler returns move ids via the event object (events can carry mutable result slots? no). 
   PRACTICAL CORRECT PATTERN used in this codebase: look at how 5.4 counts post adjustment moves — counts.py calls stock_moves.create_move DIRECTLY (inventory calling inventory). For PROCUREMENT (a different module) to cause a stock move, the sanctioned path is the event bus. So: procurement publishes GoodsReceiptPosted; inventory/handlers.py creates the moves. For the stock_move_id write-back + PO received_quantity update: KEEP those in procurement by having the handler NOT need to write back — instead, the GR line stores the move linkage via DOCFLOW (GR document → move document, queryable) rather than a stock_move_id FK column, and the PO received_quantity is updated by PROCUREMENT's own service in the same transaction AFTER publishing (procurement owns proc tables). The event is fire-and-effect; docflow is the durable link. 
   DECIDE cleanly and document in DECISIONS.md (D-041): the cross-module GR→stock-move effect goes through the event bus (procurement publishes GoodsReceiptPosted, inventory/handlers.py creates the receipt moves with the GR/IR offset in the same run_in_uow transaction); the GR↔move linkage is recorded via docflow (not a cross-module FK); procurement updates its own PO received_quantity + GR status in the same transaction; the whole chain (GR + moves + inventory-debit/GR-IR journals + PO update) commits atomically or rolls back together (closed period / insufficient handler all roll back the GR). If you find the write-back genuinely needs the move id on the GR line, drop the stock_move_id column and rely on docflow — adjust the model accordingly.
   IMPORTANT: re-validate this against STRUCTURE §5 and the existing inventory→finance pattern before coding; implement whichever is consistent. If after analysis a direct narrow call is actually how the codebase already does cross-module commands (check: does counts or anything call across modules?), follow the codebase's actual precedent and note it. The event-bus path is strongly preferred.
8. procurement router: goods_receipt_router (sibling, mounted into router.py): POST /goods-receipts (create draft; idempotent), GET /goods-receipts (paginated, filter by po/status/date), GET /goods-receipts/{id} (+lines), POST /goods-receipts/{id}/post (idempotent), POST /goods-receipts/{id}/cancel, and line management if create takes lines inline keep it simple. Permission-guard. PERFORMANCE §6.
9. Migration 0026_procurement_goods_receipts.py (down_revision 0025): the two proc tables + the valuation_offset is NOT a schema change (it's a param), the gr_ir_clearing posting purpose is data not schema. So 0026 = just the GR tables + indexes. No trigger-bearing alters.
10. docs/modules/procurement.md: goods-receipt section (the GR/IR three-way flow: GR posts Dr Inventory / Cr GR-IR; the 6.4 bill will post Dr GR-IR / Cr AP, clearing it; the event-bus cross-module mechanism; inspection-flag-only; over-receipt rejected; closed-period rollback). docs/modules/inventory.md: note the valuation_offset override. DECISIONS.md D-041.
11. Tests: backend/tests/modules/procurement/test_goods_receipts.py + test_goods_receipts_api.py: create GR draft against a PO (open-qty validation, over-receipt 422), post GR → stock RECEIPT move exists (on-hand up), inventory-debit/GR-IR journal exists (Dr inventory / Cr GR-IR, balanced, via the event), PO received_quantity raised + status PARTIALLY_RECEIVED then RECEIVED on full receipt, docflow PO→GR→move chain; closed-period receipt_date rolls the whole post back (no move, no journal, GR not posted); lot/serial receipt creates the lot/serial + lands stock; requires_inspection flag set; re-post idempotent; cancel draft-only; RBAC (manage vs post), tenant isolation, pagination, ≤3 budgets. Plus the inventory override tests (offset price-diff default vs GR/IR override). Use the query_counter; the GR post is O(lines).

RULES: no TODO/stub/dead-file; absolute imports; ruff + pytest FULLY green SQLite (`-m "not pg and not perf"`) AND `-m pg` (reset pg schema at the pg url, alembic upgrade head, run -m pg); delete stray atlas.db; every file <400 lines; comments only non-obvious; don't print file contents. Update PROGRESS.md + tick PLAN 6.3 + DECISIONS.md D-041. Run the STRUCTURE §9 self-check (esp. the §5 dependency rule — verify procurement does NOT import inventory/finance service.py) and report it.

Return: files created/changed, the EXACT cross-module mechanism you used for GR→stock-move (event-bus handler vs other) and WHY it satisfies STRUCTURE §5, how the GR/IR offset override flows, the GR/move linkage approach (docflow vs FK), the inspection-flag v1 behavior, over-receipt + closed-period handling, test counts (SQLite total+new, pg), migration number, §9 self-check, and deviations with one-line justification.

===STRUCTURE.md===
# STRUCTURE.md — Folder Structure, Naming & File-Handling Protocol for Atlas ERP

Place this file at the repo root alongside CLAUDE.md and GITHUB-WORKFLOW.md, and add to CLAUDE.md: "All file creation, naming, and placement MUST follow STRUCTURE.md. Re-read it after any compaction." The rule of this document: **every file has exactly one correct home, and its name alone tells you what's inside it.** When you are unsure where something goes, the answer is in here — do not invent a new location.

# 1. Canonical Repository Tree

```
atlas-erp/
├── CLAUDE.md  PLAN.md  PROGRESS.md  DECISIONS.md
├── GITHUB-WORKFLOW.md  STRUCTURE.md
├── README.md  LICENSE  NOTICE  CONTRIBUTING.md  SECURITY.md
├── .gitignore  .env.example  docker-compose.yml  Makefile
├── .github/
│   ├── workflows/ci.yml
│   ├── PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md
│   └── ISSUE_TEMPLATE/{bug.yaml,feature.yaml}
├── docs/
│   ├── architecture.md  api.md  industry-templates.md
│   ├── research/s4hana-parity.md
│   ├── modules/            # one guide per module: finance.md, inventory.md, ...
│   └── assets/             # diagrams/screenshots referenced by docs ONLY
├── industry-templates/
│   ├── _schema.yaml        # the template JSON-Schema, single source of truth
│   └── {manufacturing,retail,professional-services,healthcare,construction}.yaml
├── backend/
│   ├── pyproject.toml  alembic.ini
│   ├── alembic/versions/
│   ├── app/
│   │   ├── main.py         # app factory + router mounting, nothing else
│   │   ├── core/           # cross-cutting only — see §2
│   │   └── modules/        # business modules — see §3
│   ├── tests/              # mirrors app/ — see §6
│   └── seed.py
└── frontend/
    ├── package.json  vite.config.ts  tsconfig.json  index.html
    └── src/
        ├── main.tsx  App.tsx  router.tsx
        ├── lib/            # api client, auth, query hooks, formatters
        ├── components/     # design system, module-agnostic — see §4
        └── modules/        # one folder per ERP module, mirrors backend names
```

Nothing lives outside this tree. No `scratch/`, `tmp/`, `old/`, `backup/`, or `misc/` directories — ever. Temporary experiments happen on a branch and are deleted, not parked in the tree.

# 2. `backend/app/core/` — what belongs and what doesn't

One file per cross-cutting concern, flat, no subpackages: `config.py`, `db.py` (engine, session, tenant filter), `tenancy.py`, `auth.py`, `rbac.py`, `audit.py`, `events.py` (bus + base event class), `docflow.py`, `models.py` (Base, mixins: TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin), `schemas.py` (shared Pydantic bases, pagination envelope, error envelope), `numbering.py` (document sequences), `money.py` (Money/Quantity/Rate type decorators, quantize + largest-remainder allocate — added by D-015), `custom_fields.py` (custom-field defs registry, validation, JSON column helper — added by D-016), `exceptions.py`, `deps.py` (FastAPI dependencies).

**Litmus test:** if a file mentions a specific business concept (invoice, item, employee), it does NOT belong in `core/` — move it to its module. If two modules need the same business logic, the dependency-rule in §5 decides who owns it; `core/` is never the dumping ground.

# 3. `backend/app/modules/` — identical anatomy for every module

Module package names (fixed, never abbreviate differently elsewhere): `finance`, `inventory`, `procurement`, `sales`, `manufacturing`, `quality`, `maintenance`, `hr`, `projects`, `crm`, `reporting`, `admin`, `industry`.

Every module has exactly this internal shape — no exceptions, no creativity:

```
modules/finance/
├── __init__.py
├── models.py        # SQLAlchemy models (split into models/ package only if >600 lines: models/journal.py, models/accounts.py, each <400)
├── schemas.py       # Pydantic request/response (same split rule)
├── service.py       # ALL business logic (split rule: service/ package, one file per aggregate: service/journal.py, service/payments.py)
├── router.py        # thin HTTP layer only: parse → call service → return schema
├── events.py        # events this module PUBLISHES (definitions) 
├── handlers.py      # subscriptions to OTHER modules' events
└── constants.py     # enums, status values, magic numbers — no literals inline elsewhere
```

A new file type may not be invented per-module. If finance needs `depreciation.py`, it goes inside `service/` as `service/depreciation.py`, not as a new top-level module file.

# 4. Frontend structure

- `src/components/` is the design system: one folder per component (`DataGrid/`, `FormBuilder/`, `Kanban/`, `KpiCard/`, `DocFlowViewer/`), each containing `ComponentName.tsx`, optional `ComponentName.test.tsx`, and `index.ts` re-export. Components here know NOTHING about ERP concepts — they take data and callbacks.
- `src/modules/<module>/` mirrors backend module names exactly and contains: `pages/` (route components, named `<Entity>ListPage.tsx`, `<Entity>DetailPage.tsx`, `<Entity>FormPage.tsx`), `components/` (module-specific composites), `api.ts` (typed endpoint calls for this module only), `types.ts` (mirrors backend schemas), `hooks.ts` (TanStack Query hooks: `useJournalEntries`, `usePostJournal`).
- `src/lib/`: `apiClient.ts` (the ONLY place fetch/axios appears), `auth.ts`, `queryClient.ts`, `format.ts` (money, dates, quantities — all display formatting goes through here, never inline `toFixed`).
- No barrel-exporting whole modules into each other; cross-module UI reuse means the component was design-system material and must be promoted to `src/components/`.

# 5. Dependency Rules (what may import what)

- `core` imports nothing from `modules`. Modules import `core` freely.
- Modules never import each other's `service.py` or `models.py` directly. Cross-module effects go through the event bus (`finance/handlers.py` reacts to `inventory` events). Cross-module reads needed synchronously (e.g., sales needs an item's price) go through a small, explicit query interface the owning module exposes in `modules/<owner>/queries.py` — plus `modules/<owner>/events.py` (declarative event dataclasses only, no logic), the two files another module may import (events.py allowance added by D-011 so handlers can subscribe to typed events).
- Dependency direction for queries: finance is the bottom (everyone may use finance/queries), then inventory, then everything else. Two modules may never import each other's queries bidirectionally — if that seems needed, the shared concept is misplaced; file an issue and resolve ownership before coding.
- Frontend: `modules/*` may import `lib` and `components`; `components` and `lib` never import from `modules`.

# 6. Tests mirror source, exactly

`backend/tests/` replicates `app/` paths: code in `app/modules/finance/service/journal.py` is tested in `tests/modules/finance/test_journal.py`. Shared fixtures live in `tests/conftest.py` (db session, tenant factory, auth client) and `tests/modules/<module>/conftest.py` for module fixtures. Test names state the rule being proven: `test_journal_rejects_unbalanced_lines`, `test_posting_to_closed_period_raises`. One assertion-theme per test. Frontend tests sit beside the file they test (`DataGrid.test.tsx`). A regression test for issue #NN includes `#NN` in its docstring/comment.

# 7. Naming Conventions (single table of truth)

| Thing | Convention | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Python files/modules | snake_case, singular concern | `journal.py`, `stock_move.py` |
| Python classes | PascalCase, no abbreviations | `JournalEntry`, `StockMove`, `PurchaseOrderLine` |
| Python functions/vars | snake_case verbs for actions | `post_journal_entry()`, `reserve_stock()` |
| Pydantic schemas | Entity + suffix `Create/Update/Read/Filter` | `JournalEntryCreate`, `ItemRead` |
| DB tables | snake_case plural, module prefix | `fin_journal_entries`, `inv_stock_moves`, `sls_orders` |
| DB columns | snake_case; FKs `<entity>_id`; money pairs `amount`+`currency_code`; booleans `is_/has_` | `is_posted`, `cost_center_id` |
| Enums (Py + DB values) | Class PascalCase, values UPPER_SNAKE stored as strings | `OrderStatus.PARTIALLY_SHIPPED` |
| Alembic revisions | `NNNN_short_description` sequential | `0007_add_asset_register` |
| Domain events | PascalCase past tense, module-prefixed string key | class `SalesOrderShipped`, key `sales.order.shipped` |
| Permissions | `module.entity.action` lowercase | `finance.journal.post` |
| API routes | `/api/v1/<module>/<resource-kebab-plural>`; actions as sub-resources, never verbs in resource names | `/api/v1/finance/journal-entries/{id}/post` |
| JSON fields | snake_case (mirror backend; frontend types match, no camelCase translation layer) | `posting_date` |
| TS files | Components PascalCase.tsx, everything else camelCase.ts | `DataGrid.tsx`, `apiClient.ts` |
| TS types/interfaces | PascalCase, no `I` prefix | `JournalEntry` |
| React hooks | `use` + Entity + verb | `usePostJournalEntry` |
| CSS | Tailwind utilities only; the rare custom class kebab-case in one `index.css` | `doc-flow-edge` |
| Env vars | `ATLAS_` prefix UPPER_SNAKE | `ATLAS_DATABASE_URL` |
| Docs files | kebab-case | `industry-templates.md` |
| Branches/commits/labels | as defined in GITHUB-WORKFLOW.md | — |

Terminology lock: the same business concept uses the same word everywhere — code, DB, API, UI, docs. It is `item` (not product/article/sku interchangeably), `vendor` (not supplier), `customer`, `warehouse`, `journal entry`. Industry templates may override the *display* label, never the internal name. Record any new canonical term in DECISIONS.md the moment you coin it.

# 8. File-Handling Rules

1. **Search before create.** Before creating any file, check whether its correct home already exists (`ls`, `grep -r "class JournalEntry"`). Duplicate implementations are a `severity:major` issue.
2. **No versioned filenames.** Never `service_v2.py`, `utils_new.py`, `final_fixed.tsx`. Improving a file means editing it; git holds history.
3. **No orphan files.** Every file is imported/referenced by something or it doesn't exist. When refactoring away from a file, delete it in the same commit.
4. **Size limits.** Hard cap 400 lines per Python file and 300 per TSX component; at the cap, split along the rules in §3/§4 — never split into `part1/part2`.
5. **One concept per file.** A file named `journal.py` containing tax logic is misfiled even if it compiles. Filename promises content.
6. **Generated files are never hand-edited** (OpenAPI dumps, lockfiles, migration auto-generations get reviewed and adjusted only through their tooling). Commit lockfiles; never commit build output, caches, coverage reports, or `__pycache__` — keep `.gitignore` authoritative.
7. **No utils graveyards.** Before adding to a `utils`-like file, ask which module/concern owns the function; `core/` files and `lib/format.ts` are the only sanctioned shared helpers, each scoped by its filename.
8. **Imports:** absolute imports only in backend (`from app.modules.finance.service import journal`); frontend uses the `@/` alias (`@/lib/apiClient`). No relative `../../..` chains.
9. **Module READMEs are forbidden** — module docs live in `docs/modules/<module>.md` only, so documentation has one home.
10. **Renames/moves** are their own commit (`refactor(structure): move costing into inventory/service/costing.py`), never mixed with logic changes, so history stays traceable.
11. **Deletions** follow issue-first if the file contains live logic being retired: file the issue, explain replacement, delete in the fix PR.
12. **After compaction:** before creating ANY new file, re-read this document and run `git status` + `tree -L 3` (or `find`) to re-anchor on the actual current structure. Never recreate from memory a file that might already exist.

# 9. Self-Check (append result to PROGRESS.md at each session end)

Any file outside the canonical tree? Any file over the size cap? Any duplicate concept names (`grep` a few suspects)? Any orphan files? Any module breaking the dependency rules? Any term drift (supplier vs vendor)? Each "yes" becomes a `tech-debt` issue per GITHUB-WORKFLOW.md §6, fixed before the next promotion.

429	## D-020 — Inventory costing (moving average + FIFO layers, same-transaction COGS, no negative stock)
430	
431	**Decision.**
432	`inv_items.costing_method` enum MOVING_AVERAGE|FIFO, defaulted from item category, changeable only while no stock exists. Quantity SSOT remains `inv_stock_moves`.
433	
434	**Moving average:** `inv_item_valuations` (tenant_id, item_id, warehouse_id, on_hand_qty QuantityType, avg_unit_cost full-precision, total_value MoneyType; UNIQUE(tenant_id, item_id, warehouse_id)), updated in the SAME transaction as the move under `select(...).with_for_update()` — on Postgres this takes the row lock serializing concurrent movers; on SQLite the dialect silently OMITS the FOR UPDATE clause (it is a no-op, not an error — clarified from the drafts' contradictory claims), and SQLite's single-writer lock provides equivalent serialization; the PG locking path is proven by pg-marked concurrency tests in CI.
435	- Receipt: `total_value += receipt_value; on_hand_qty += qty; avg_unit_cost = total_value / on_hand_qty` unrounded.
436	- Issue: `cogs = quantize(qty × avg_unit_cost, currency dp, HALF_UP); total_value -= cogs`; when on_hand_qty hits 0, residual total_value is flushed to the price-difference account so value and quantity never disagree.
437	
438	**FIFO:** `inv_cost_layers` (id, tenant_id, item_id, warehouse_id, receipt_move_id FK, received_at, original_qty, remaining_qty with CHECK `remaining_qty >= 0 AND remaining_qty <= original_qty`, unit_cost) plus `inv_layer_consumptions` (issue_move_id, layer_id, qty, cost). Issues consume layers ordered (received_at, id) ascending under `with_for_update`, one consumption row per touched layer; COGS = sum of per-layer quantized qty × unit_cost. Reversing an issue replays consumption rows backwards onto the exact layers; vendor returns consume layers normally; customer returns create a new layer at original COGS cost.
439	
440	**COGS consistency:** the in-process bus dispatches synchronously in the SAME session/transaction — inventory writes move + valuation/layer updates, publishes `inventory.stock.issued` carrying the computed cost and dimensions; `finance/handlers.py` posts the COGS journal entry (Dr COGS / Cr Inventory, dimensions copied: item, warehouse, cost center/WBS) before commit. One commit = move + valuation + journal + docflow link; a stock move can never exist without its journal entry or vice versa — explicitly recorded as the v1 decision whose future Kafka swap introduces a transactional outbox then, not now.
441	
442	**Negative stock forbidden outright:** service raises InsufficientStockError pre-flight, DB CHECKs (`on_hand_qty >= 0`, `remaining_qty >= 0`) back it; no per-warehouse opt-in. **Deadlock avoidance:** any transaction touching multiple valuation rows locks in (item_id, warehouse_id) sort order.
443	
444	**Rationale.**
445	The parity doc commits to moving average AND FIFO per item category with event-driven COGS posting. Same-transaction handling is the only design keeping stock value in the journal identical to the valuation table without reconciliation machinery, while the bus abstraction still decouples the modules at code level per CLAUDE.md rule 6. Layer consumption rows make COGS auditable per layer and reversals exact rather than recomputed. Banning negative stock makes FIFO well-defined and keeps the valuation CHECKs simple; shortage handling belongs to ATP/backorders per the parity doc.
446	
447	**Rejected alternatives.**
448	- Async/after-commit COGS: opens a stock-vs-GL divergence window requiring reconciliation jobs that contradict the universal-journal philosophy.
449	- Negative stock with provisional cost and retroactive correction (Odoo-style): requires retroactive revaluation clashing with posted-entry immutability.
450	- Global valuation row without warehouse dimension: parity scope is multi-warehouse and transfers need per-warehouse value.
451	- Report-time FIFO COGS recomputation: COGS must be a posted journal fact or statements change as layers mutate.
452	
453	**Risks & mitigations.**
454	- A finance handler bug rolls back inventory operations — intended (correctness over availability), documented for operators, tightly tested on the handler path.
455	- Moving-average rounding drift — absorbed by the zero-quantity flush rule, tested explicitly.
456	- SQLite cannot exercise true lock contention — accepted; the pg-marked tests carry that burden in CI.
457	
458	---
459	
460	## D-021 — Statements as pure projections + account-type model
461	
462	**Decision.**
463	`fin_accounts` (tenant_id, code, name, account_type ASSET|LIABILITY|EQUITY|REVENUE|EXPENSE, normal_balance derived from type, is_postable, cash_flow_category nullable OPERATING|INVESTING|FINANCING, is_cash_equivalent, account_group_id FK); `fin_account_groups` (tenant_id, code, name, parent_id self-FK, sort_order) as a pure presentation hierarchy; only leaf accounts postable.
464	
465	All statements build in `finance/service/statements.py` (reporting consumes via `finance/queries.py`) from ONE base aggregate over `fin_journal_lines` only — no header join, because lines denormalize tenant_id, posting_date, fiscal_period_id, is_posted (set during the posting transaction):
466	
467	```python
468	select(JournalLine.account_id,
469	       func.sum(functional_debit_amount - functional_credit_amount))
470	.where(tenant filter, is_posted == True, date predicates)
471	.group_by(account_id)
472	```
473	
474	MoneyType type propagation keeps sums exact on both backends.
475	
476	- **Trial balance** = that query split into per-account debit/credit totals.
477	- **P&L** = REVENUE+EXPENSE over a range.
478	- **Balance sheet** = ASSET/LIABILITY/EQUITY cumulative to a date, with retained earnings computed on the fly as cumulative REVENUE+EXPENSE net over ALL history to the as-of date, presented as a synthetic "Current and accumulated earnings" equity line (exact by construction, since v1 has no year-end carryforward per the parity doc).
479	- **Cash flow (indirect)** = net income + signed deltas of non-cash balance-sheet balances between two as-of dates grouped by cash_flow_category, with the service ASSERTING reconciliation to the movement on is_cash_equivalent accounts equals zero — a built-in self-check.
480	
481	**No stored totals anywhere:** no balance tables, no materialized views (CLAUDE.md rule 1).
482	
483	**Performance:** composite partial index `ix_fin_journal_lines_proj` ON (tenant_id, account_id, posting_date), declared with BOTH `postgresql_where=is_posted` AND `sqlite_where=is_posted` dialect kwargs (each engine needs its own — added; the draft named only one), plus `postgresql_include=['functional_debit_amount','functional_credit_amount']` for index-only scans on PG (kwarg harmlessly ignored on SQLite). Holds sub-second to ~10M lines on Postgres. Escape hatch if scale exceeds that: an explicitly-cache-semantics materialized view refreshed from the journal (journal stays SSOT), out of v1 and gated on a DECISIONS.md entry.
484	
485	The is_posted flag's agreement with header status is guaranteed by the two-flush posting protocol plus immutability triggers and asserted by a dedicated guard test.
486	
487	**Rationale.**
488	Direct implementation of the Universal Journal rule: views are projections, totals never stored, FI/CO reconciliation eliminated by construction. Five account types + cash_flow_category is the minimal metadata from which all four statements derive mechanically; computing retained earnings from full history is what makes "no carryforward in v1" sound rather than a correctness hole. One base query keeps every statement provably consistent with the trial balance — same predicate, same index.
489	
490	**Rejected alternatives.**
491	- Running-balance or period-totals tables updated on posting: violates CLAUDE.md rule 1 verbatim and reintroduces reconciliation.
492	- Account-code-range statement layout (classic SAP FSV intervals): the account_group FK hierarchy is simpler, referentially enforced, template-friendly.
493	- Direct cash-flow method: requires counterparty-cash tagging on every line; indirect derives from data already present.
494	- Materialized views in v1: premature and PG-only.
495	
496	**Risks & mitigations.**
497	- Cumulative-from-genesis balance-sheet queries grow linearly with history until balance carryforward ships (already a parity-doc "later") — the partial covering index keeps this an index-only scan on PG, and the carryforward job slots in later without schema change.
498	
499	---
500	
501	## D-022 — Alembic dual-database strategy and CI matrix
502	
503	**Decision.**
504	A single linear migration chain runs unmodified on both backends; migrations are the ONLY schema source — `Base.metadata.create_all` is banned everywhere INCLUDING tests, because triggers and raw DDL live only in migrations (tests would otherwise pass without the DB guards they claim to test). Rules:
505	
506	1. `env.py` uses the async pattern (`async_engine_from_config` + `connection.run_sync(do_run_migrations)`, `asyncio.run` in the offline-safe wrapper), reads `ATLAS_DATABASE_URL`, configures `compare_type=True` and `render_as_batch=True`.
507	2. Every ALTER goes through `with op.batch_alter_table(...)` unconditionally — pass-through on Postgres, copy-rebuild on SQLite — which requires deterministic constraint names: `core/models.py` declares `MetaData(naming_convention={'ix':'ix_%(column_0_label)s','uq':'uq_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_name)s','ck':'ck_%(table_name)s_%(constraint_name)s','fk':'fk_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_name)s_%(referred_table_name)s','pk':'pk_%(table_name)s'})`; unnamed constraints cannot be dropped in SQLite batch mode.
508	3. Type portability lives in the models (`with_variant` JSONB, `sa.Uuid`, MoneyType/QuantityType/RateType), so autogenerated revisions import those types from `app.core.models` and stay dialect-clean; hand review of every autogen revision is mandatory.
509	4. Trigger/function DDL: per-dialect string pairs side by side in the migration body under `if op.get_bind().dialect.name == 'postgresql': op.execute(PG_SQL) else: op.execute(SQLITE_SQL)`; stable names `trg_<table>_<purpose>`; upgrades DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS then CREATE; downgrades drop. **Rule (load-bearing):** any migration that batch-alters a trigger-bearing table MUST re-execute that table's trigger DDL afterwards, because SQLite's copy-rebuild silently drops triggers — recorded in the migration template comment and caught by the guard tests, which run against the final migrated schema. Postgres-only physical extras (GIN indexes, INCLUDE columns) sit in the same dialect branch with a plain-index or no-op SQLite arm.
510	5. CI, single `backend` job extended: **step A** `alembic upgrade head` + full `uv run pytest -q` on SQLite (file DB); **step B** `services: postgres:16` container — `alembic upgrade head`, then `alembic downgrade base && alembic upgrade head` (reversibility proof), then `uv run pytest -q -m pg` re-exercising the DB-guard subset (journal/period/audit triggers, JSONB paths, with_for_update contention, idempotency races) on real Postgres. The `pg` marker lives on `tests/modules/finance/test_journal_db_guards.py`, period bypass tests, audit append-only tests, and inventory locking tests.
511	
512	**Rationale.**
513	D-003 fixed the dual-backend posture; this makes it mechanical. Batch-everywhere plus a naming convention is the canonical Alembic SQLite recipe; model-level type variance makes autogenerate output portable by construction; and running the financial-guard tests on real Postgres is what turns "enforced at DB level on BOTH" from an assertion into a tested claim. The trigger-recreation-after-batch rule prevents the silent-guard-loss failure mode that would otherwise pass every test until a rebuild migration ships.
514	
515	**Rejected alternatives.**
516	- Two migration branches per dialect: guaranteed drift, doubled review, breaks linear NNNN numbering.
517	- `create_all` for tests with a trigger fixture: duplicates trigger DDL outside migrations, violating single-source.
518	- Skipping Postgres in CI: trigger and FOR UPDATE behavior differ enough that untested-on-PG is unacceptable for the financial engine.
519	- Separate .sql files for trigger DDL: STRUCTURE forbids orphan files; migrations are self-contained.
520	
521	**Risks & mitigations.**
522	- Per-test isolation against the migrated schema is owned by D-025 (template-copy pattern) — the two decisions interlock and must not drift.
523	- Autogen occasionally emits dialect-specific DDL despite variants — mandatory hand review per STRUCTURE §8.6 plus the dual-engine CI run catches it.
524	
525	---
526	
527	## D-023 — Frontend type strategy (hand-written types.ts with compile-time drift gate)
528	
529	**Decision.**
530	Per STRUCTURE §4, each frontend module keeps a HAND-WRITTEN `src/modules/<module>/types.ts` mirroring that module's backend Pydantic Read/Create/Update/Filter schemas, snake_case preserved (no camelCase translation layer).
531	
532	**Mapping conventions, fixed:** Decimal/money → `string`; date/datetime → `string` (ISO 8601); UUID → `string`; backend enums → TS string-literal unions of the UPPER_SNAKE values (`type EntryStatus = 'DRAFT' | 'POSTED' | 'REVERSED'`); nullable/Optional → `| null`; Masked fields → `T | null`. Shared envelope types (`Page<T> {items, next_cursor, limit}`, `ApiError {error: {code, message, details, request_id}}`) live once in `src/lib/apiClient.ts`.
533	
534	**Drift control, two compile-time gates and zero runtime cost:**
535	
536	1. `backend/openapi.json` is COMMITTED and regenerated via a Makefile target (`make openapi` calls a tiny dump entry that instantiates the app factory and writes `app.openapi()`); a backend pytest test asserts the committed file equals the live app's schema, so any schema change that forgets regeneration fails the backend CI job with a "run make openapi" message.
537	2. A frontend devDependency `openapi-typescript` generates a GITIGNORED `src/lib/openapi.gen.d.ts` from `../backend/openapi.json` as a pre-step of `npm run typecheck`; each module adds a `types.contract.ts` containing only type-level assertions using Expect/Equal helpers from lib (`type _ = Expect<Equal<JournalEntry, components['schemas']['JournalEntryRead']>>`) — one line per mirrored type — so tsc fails on any divergence in either direction.
538

1	"""The stock-move WRITE engine (PLAN 5.2, D-020/D-036): create_move (the heart) + reverse_move.
2	
3	The read paths (``get_move``, ``list_moves``, ``list_on_hand``) live in ``stock_reads.py`` (split at
4	the 400-line cap); this module imports ``get_move`` from there and the package ``__init__``
5	re-exports both halves as one surface.
6	
7	A stock move is the quantity SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH and is POSTED-at-creation + IMMUTABLE — there
8	is no draft phase, no edit, no delete; a correction is a NEW reversing move (the universal-journal
9	reversal philosophy of D-017 applied to stock). ``create_move``:
10	
11	1. validates — item is STOCKED; the move_type's required bin sides are present (constants
12	   MOVE_BIN_SIDES; ADJUSTMENT = exactly one side; TRANSFER = two DIFFERENT bins); bins exist and
13	   belong to ACTIVE warehouses; quantity > 0; the item's tracking mode is satisfied (lot/serial
14	   resolved, created on a receipt, required-existing on issue/transfer; serial ⇒ quantity == 1);
15	2. registers the document + claims the gapless STK number (D-012, at creation — a move is permanent
16	   at create);
17	3. inserts the StockMove (POSTED);
18	4. updates the quant rows in the SAME transaction — decrement from_bin, increment to_bin — through
19	   ``apply_bin_delta`` (the CHECK >= 0 + the pre-flight check forbid negative stock, D-020);
20	   transfer deltas are applied in deterministic bin-id order (deadlock avoidance, D-020).
21	
22	The whole thing is one unit of work: move + quant updates commit or roll back together, so the
23	ledger and the projection can never disagree. Idempotency (D-013) is owned by the endpoint.
24	Inventory imports only finance/queries downward (STRUCTURE §5); this engine imports neither.
25	"""

62	async def _require_stocked_item(
63	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID
64	) -> Item:
65	    item = await session.get(Item, item_id)
66	    if item is None or item.tenant_id != tenant_id:
67	        raise NotFoundError(message="Item not found", code="inventory.item_not_found")
68	    if ItemType(item.item_type) != ItemType.STOCKED:
69	        raise ValidationFailedError(

71	            code="inventory.item_not_stocked",
72	            details={"item_id": str(item_id), "item_type": item.item_type},
73	        )

77	async def _require_active_bin(
78	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, bin_id: uuid.UUID, *, side: str
79	) -> Bin:
80	    """The bin exists, belongs to this tenant, and its warehouse is active. A move never lands stock
81	    in (or pulls from) a bin whose warehouse was deactivated."""
82	    bin_row = await session.get(Bin, bin_id)
83	    if bin_row is None or bin_row.tenant_id != tenant_id:

98	def _validate_bin_sides(

231	        item,

233	        lot_code=payload.lot_code,
234	        create_if_missing=create_instance,
235	    )
236	    serial_id = await resolve_serial(
237	        session,
238	        tenant_id,
239	        item,

241	        serial_code=payload.serial_code,
242	        create_if_missing=create_instance,
243	    )
244	    if TrackingMode(item.tracking_mode) == TrackingMode.SERIAL and quantity != 1:
245	        raise ValidationFailedError(
246	            message="A serial-tracked move has quantity 1 (a serial moves wholesale)",
247	            code="inventory.serial_quantity_invalid",

250	
251	    move_date = payload.move_date or date.today()
252	    move_id = uuid.uuid4()
253	    document = await docflow.register_document(
254	        session,
255	        tenant_id,
256	        STOCK_MOVE_DOC_TYPE,
257	        move_id,
258	        doc_number=None,
259	        status=MoveStatus.POSTED.value,
260	    )
261	    # A move is permanent at creation (POSTED immediately), so the number is claimed now (D-012
262	    # claim-at-permanence, the orders/receipts branch, not the draft branch).
263	    await ensure_sequence(
264	        session,
265	        tenant_id,
266	        STOCK_MOVE_SEQUENCE_NAME,
267	        STOCK_MOVE_NUMBER_PREFIX,
268	        STOCK_MOVE_NUMBER_PADDING,
269	        year_reset=True,
270	    )

272	        session, tenant_id, STOCK_MOVE_SEQUENCE_NAME, on_date=move_date
273	    )

300	    )

303	        tenant_id,

305	        lot_id,

309	    )
310	    # Costing IN THE SAME TRANSACTION (D-020), right after the quant update: update the
311	    # moving-average valuation / FIFO layers, write the computed cost onto the move, and publish the
312	    # StockValued event BEFORE the uow drains it — the COGS/inventory journal posts in this same
313	    # transaction, so the move + quant + valuation + journal commit or roll back as one. A
314	    # value-neutral within-warehouse transfer returns no event (no journal).
315	    if reversal_of is not None:

318	        )

326	async def reverse_move(
327	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, move_id: uuid.UUID
328	) -> StockMove:
329	    """Reverse a posted move by posting an OPPOSITE move (PLAN 5.2): same item/quantity/lot/serial
330	    with from_bin and to_bin SWAPPED, linked to the original via docflow ('reverses'). The ledger
331	    stays append-only — corrections are new moves, never edits (D-017 philosophy). The reversing
332	    move restores the quants the original changed; a reversal that would itself go negative (the
333	    stock already left) raises InsufficientStockError like any other move. A move may be reversed
334	    once (a second reverse of the same original is rejected)."""
335	    original = await get_move(session, tenant_id, move_id)
336	    # Guard against double-reversal: a reversing move points back via docflow 'reverses'. Cheap
337	    # check — has any move already reversed this one?
338	    if await _already_reversed(session, tenant_id, original.document_id):
339	        raise ConflictError(
340	            message="This stock move has already been reversed",
341	            code="inventory.move_already_reversed",
342	        )
343	
344	    reversal_payload = StockMoveCreate(
345	        move_type=MoveType(original.move_type),
346	        item_id=original.item_id,
347	        quantity=Decimal(original.quantity),
348	        # Swap the directions so the reversing move undoes the original's quant deltas.
349	        from_bin_id=original.to_bin_id,
350	        to_bin_id=original.from_bin_id,
351	        lot_id=original.lot_id,
352	        serial_id=original.serial_id,
353	        move_date=date.today(),
354	        reference=f"Reversal of {original.move_number}",
355	    )
356	    # A reversal of a RECEIPT swaps to an ISSUE-shaped move (from set, to NULL) and vice versa; for
357	    # ADJUSTMENT/TRANSFER the swap stays the same move_type. The bin-side validator accepts the
358	    # swapped shape because the move_type's required side follows the populated bin.
359	    reversal_payload = _retype_for_reversal(reversal_payload, MoveType(original.move_type))
360	
361	    # Pass the original so create_move runs the costing REVERSAL (replay), not a fresh valuation,
362	    # and
363	    # publishes the OPPOSITE StockValued event so the COGS journal is reversed in the same
364	    # transaction (D-020).
365	    reversal = await create_move(
366	        session, tenant_id, reversal_payload, reversal_of=original
367	    )
368	    await docflow.link_documents(
369	        session,
370	        tenant_id,
371	        predecessor=original.document_id,
372	        successor=reversal.document_id,
373	        link_type=STOCK_MOVE_REVERSES_LINK,
374	    )
375	    return reversal
376	
377	
378	def _retype_for_reversal(payload: StockMoveCreate, original_type: MoveType) -> StockMoveCreate:
379	    """A RECEIPT reverses as an ISSUE and an ISSUE as a RECEIPT (the bin sides flip, so the type
380	    must too, or the bin-side validator rejects the swapped shape). TRANSFER and ADJUSTMENT keep
381	    their type — a swapped TRANSFER is still a TRANSFER, and a swapped ADJUSTMENT (the single side
382	    moves to the other side) is still an ADJUSTMENT."""
383	    if original_type == MoveType.RECEIPT:
384	        return payload.model_copy(update={"move_type": MoveType.ISSUE})
385	    if original_type == MoveType.ISSUE:
386	        return payload.model_copy(update={"move_type": MoveType.RECEIPT})
387	    return payload
388	
389	
390	async def _already_reversed(
391	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, document_id: uuid.UUID
392	) -> bool:
393	    """Whether a 'reverses' edge already points FROM this move's document (it has been reversed)."""
394	    chain = await docflow.get_document_chain(session, tenant_id, document_id)
395	    return any(
396	        edge.link_type == STOCK_MOVE_REVERSES_LINK
397	        and edge.predecessor_document_id == document_id
398	        for edge in chain.edges
399	    )

1	"""The costing engine (PLAN 5.3, D-020/D-037): moving-average AND FIFO valuation per (item,
2	warehouse), computed in the SAME transaction as the stock move, right after the quant update and
3	BEFORE the move's costing event is published.
4	
5	The move ledger + quants stay the QUANTITY SSOT; ``inv_item_valuations`` (moving-average) and
6	``inv_cost_layers`` + ``inv_layer_consumptions`` (FIFO) are the VALUE SSOT (D-037). Which engine a
7	(item, warehouse) uses is the item's ``costing_method``.
8	
9	``apply_costing`` is the single entry point ``create_move`` calls. It:
10	1. resolves the move's direction + warehouse(s) from its bins,
11	2. runs the moving-average or FIFO update (receipt adds value, issue computes + removes it),
12	3. writes the computed cost back onto the move (``unit_cost``),
13	4. returns a ``CostingResult`` carrying the ``StockValued`` event (or None for a value-neutral
14	   within-warehouse transfer) for ``create_move`` to publish.
15	
16	Reversal: ``reverse_costing`` undoes a move's valuation symmetrically — a reversed ISSUE replays its
17	FIFO consumptions backward / re-adds moving-average value; a reversed RECEIPT zeros its layer /
18	removes moving-average value. The reversing move publishes the OPPOSITE costing event so the COGS
19	journal is reversed too.
20	
21	The moving-average row math lives in ``costing_mav.py`` and the FIFO layer mechanics in
22	``costing_fifo.py`` (split at the 400-line cap); this file owns the orchestration + reversal
23	sequencing + the StockValued event build.
24	"""
25	
26	from __future__ import annotations
27	
28	import uuid
29	from dataclasses import dataclass
30	from decimal import Decimal
31	
32	from sqlalchemy import select
33	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
34	
35	from app.core.exceptions import ValidationFailedError
36	from app.modules.finance import queries as finance_queries
37	from app.modules.inventory import queries as inventory_queries
38	from app.modules.inventory.constants import (
39	    DEFAULT_COSTING_CURRENCY,
40	    CostingMethod,
41	    MoveType,
42	)

48	@dataclass(frozen=True)
49	class CostingResult:
50	    """What ``apply_costing`` produced for one move: the computed unit cost (written onto the move)
51	    and the ``StockValued`` event to publish (None when the move moved no value — a within-warehouse
52	    transfer — so no journal is posted, D-037)."""
53	
54	    unit_cost: Decimal | None
55	    event: StockValued | None

58	async def _warehouse_of_bin(
59	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, bin_id: uuid.UUID
60	) -> uuid.UUID:
61	    """The warehouse a bin belongs to (valuation is per warehouse, not per bin — D-037). The bin was
62	    already validated by the move engine, so a missing one here is an invariant break, not user
63	    input."""
64	    warehouse_id = (
65	        await session.execute(
66	            select(Bin.warehouse_id).where(
67	                Bin.tenant_id == tenant_id, Bin.id == bin_id
68	            )
69	        )
70	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
71	    if warehouse_id is None:

73	            message="The bin has no warehouse for valuation",
74	            code="inventory.costing_bin_warehouse_missing",
75	            details={"bin_id": str(bin_id)},
76	        )

80	async def _costing_currency(session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID) -> str:
81	    """The currency the COGS/inventory journal posts in (D-015): the tenant's functional currency
82	    when configured, else the v1 single-currency default. Costs quantize to its decimals."""
83	    func_code = await finance_queries.functional_currency_or_none(session, tenant_id)
84	    return func_code or DEFAULT_COSTING_CURRENCY
85	
86	
87	async def _category_accounts(
88	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID
89	) -> tuple[uuid.UUID, uuid.UUID, uuid.UUID]:
90	    """The item category's three GL account ids (inventory, COGS, price-difference), REQUIRED before
91	    a stocked move can value (D-020/D-029). A STOCKED item whose category has not wired them cannot
92	    post a move — the value would have nowhere to land — so this raises a clear 422."""
93	    accounts = await inventory_queries.get_category_accounts(session, tenant_id, item_id)
94	    if accounts is None or any(account_id is None for account_id in accounts):
95	        raise ValidationFailedError(
96	            message="The item's category must wire inventory, COGS and price-difference accounts "
97	            "before stock can be valued",
98	            code="inventory.category_accounts_unwired",
99	            details={"item_id": str(item_id)},
100	        )
101	    return accounts  # type: ignore[return-value]
102

104	# --- Orchestration ------------------------------------------------------------

107	async def apply_costing(
108	    session: AsyncSession,
109	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
110	    item: Item,
111	    move: StockMove,
112	) -> CostingResult:
113	    """Run costing for a just-created move IN THE SAME TRANSACTION (D-020), after the quant update.
114	
115	    Resolves direction + warehouse(s), runs the moving-average or FIFO engine, writes the computed
116	    ``unit_cost`` back onto the move, and returns the ``StockValued`` event for ``create_move`` to
117	    publish (None for a value-neutral within-warehouse transfer). RECEIPT/positive-ADJUSTMENT use
118	    the
119	    move's passed ``unit_cost`` (the entry cost); ISSUE/negative-ADJUSTMENT IGNORE it and
120	    compute."""
121	    move_type = MoveType(move.move_type)
122	    qty = Decimal(move.quantity)
123	    method = CostingMethod(item.costing_method)
124	    currency_code = await _costing_currency(session, tenant_id)
125	    accounts = await _category_accounts(session, tenant_id, item.id)
126	
127	    from_warehouse_id = (
128	        await _warehouse_of_bin(session, tenant_id, move.from_bin_id)
129	        if move.from_bin_id is not None
130	        else None
131	    )
132	    to_warehouse_id = (
133	        await _warehouse_of_bin(session, tenant_id, move.to_bin_id)
134	        if move.to_bin_id is not None
135	        else None
136	    )
137	
138	    if move_type == MoveType.TRANSFER:
139	        return await _apply_transfer(
140	            session, tenant_id, item, move, qty, method, currency_code,
141	            from_warehouse_id, to_warehouse_id,
142	        )
143	
144	    # Direction is structural: a populated to_bin warehouse is inbound (RECEIPT / increase), a
145	    # populated from_bin warehouse is outbound (ISSUE / decrease). ADJUSTMENT sets exactly one side.
146	    if to_warehouse_id is not None:
147	        return await _apply_inbound(
148	            session, tenant_id, item, move, qty, method, to_warehouse_id, accounts
149	        )
150	    if from_warehouse_id is not None:
151	        return await _apply_outbound(
152	            session, tenant_id, item, move, qty, method, currency_code,
153	            from_warehouse_id, accounts,
154	        )
155	    raise ValidationFailedError(
156	        message="The move has no warehouse side to value",
157	        code="inventory.costing_no_side",
158	        details={"move_id": str(move.id)},
159	    )

162	async def _apply_inbound(
163	    session: AsyncSession,
164	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
165	    item: Item,
166	    move: StockMove,
167	    qty: Decimal,
168	    method: CostingMethod,
169	    warehouse_id: uuid.UUID,
170	    accounts: tuple[uuid.UUID, uuid.UUID, uuid.UUID],
171	) -> CostingResult:
172	    """RECEIPT / positive ADJUSTMENT: stock enters at the move's REQUIRED ``unit_cost`` (the entry
173	    cost). Updates the moving-average row or creates a FIFO layer, and emits a value-increasing
174	    StockValued event the handler posts as Dr inventory."""
175	    unit_cost = _require_entry_cost(move)
176	    total_cost = qty * unit_cost
177	    if method == CostingMethod.MOVING_AVERAGE:
178	        await costing_mav.mav_receive(session, tenant_id, item.id, warehouse_id, qty, unit_cost)
179	    else:
180	        await costing_fifo.create_layer(
181	            session,
182	            tenant_id,
183	            item_id=item.id,
184	            warehouse_id=warehouse_id,
185	            receipt_move_id=move.id,
186	            received_at=move.move_date,
187	            qty=qty,

189	        )

191	    inventory_account_id, _cogs_account_id, price_diff_account_id = accounts
192	    # A receipt / stock-increase offsets to the price-difference (inventory-adjustment) account: a
193	    # STANDALONE receipt has no procurement GR clearing yet (procurement overrides this later, 6.x).
194	    event = _build_event(
195	        move, warehouse_id, qty, total_cost, Decimal(0),
196	        inventory_account_id, price_diff_account_id, price_diff_account_id,
197	        is_inbound=True,
198	    )
199	    return CostingResult(unit_cost=unit_cost, event=event)

202	async def _apply_outbound(
203	    session: AsyncSession,
204	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
205	    item: Item,
206	    move: StockMove,
207	    qty: Decimal,
208	    method: CostingMethod,
209	    currency_code: str,
210	    warehouse_id: uuid.UUID,
211	    accounts: tuple[uuid.UUID, uuid.UUID, uuid.UUID],
212	) -> CostingResult:
213	    """ISSUE / negative ADJUSTMENT: the engine COMPUTES the cost of the stock that left (the passed
214	    unit_cost is ignored). Moving average quantizes qty × avg + flushes residual at zero on-hand;
215	    FIFO sums per-layer quantized costs. Emits a value-decreasing StockValued event the handler
216	    posts
217	    as Dr COGS / Cr inventory."""
218	    residual_flush = Decimal(0)
219	    if method == CostingMethod.MOVING_AVERAGE:
220	        cogs, residual_flush = await costing_mav.mav_issue(
221	            session, tenant_id, item.id, warehouse_id, qty, currency_code
222	        )
223	    else:
224	        cogs = await costing_fifo.consume_layers(

226	            tenant_id,

229	            issue_move_id=move.id,

231	            currency_code=currency_code,
232	        )

234	    move.unit_cost = unit_cost
235	    inventory_account_id, cogs_account_id, price_diff_account_id = accounts
236	    # An ISSUE charges COGS (goods left for sale/production); an ADJUSTMENT-down is an inventory
237	    # write-off with no document behind it, so it offsets to the price-difference account (D-020).
238	    offset_account_id = (
239	        cogs_account_id
240	        if MoveType(move.move_type) == MoveType.ISSUE
241	        else price_diff_account_id
242	    )
243	    event = _build_event(
244	        move, warehouse_id, qty, cogs, residual_flush,
245	        inventory_account_id, offset_account_id, price_diff_account_id,
246	        is_inbound=False,
247	    )

251	async def _apply_transfer(
252	    session: AsyncSession,
253	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
254	    item: Item,
255	    move: StockMove,
256	    qty: Decimal,
257	    method: CostingMethod,
258	    currency_code: str,
259	    from_warehouse_id: uuid.UUID | None,
260	    to_warehouse_id: uuid.UUID | None,
261	) -> CostingResult:
262	    """TRANSFER carries cost at the current valuation. Within ONE warehouse it is fully
263	    value-neutral — the valuation/layers don't change and NO journal is posted (D-037). Between
264	    warehouses the value moves WITH the stock (issue from source at current cost, receive into dest
265	    at that same cost) but, because both warehouses share the one inventory account in v1, the net
266	    journal is still zero — so a transfer never publishes a StockValued event. The computed transfer
267	    unit cost is still written onto the move for the ledger."""
268	    if from_warehouse_id is None or to_warehouse_id is None:
269	        raise ValidationFailedError(
270	            message="A transfer needs both warehouses to value",
271	            code="inventory.costing_transfer_sides",
272	            details={"move_id": str(move.id)},
273	        )
274	    if from_warehouse_id == to_warehouse_id:
275	        # Same warehouse: only the bin changed; value is unchanged. Carry the current cost onto the
276	        # move for the ledger, touch nothing else, post no journal.
277	        move.unit_cost = await _current_unit_cost(
278	            session, tenant_id, item, from_warehouse_id, method
279	        )
280	        return CostingResult(unit_cost=move.unit_cost, event=None)
281	
282	    # Cross-warehouse: remove value from the source and add it to the destination at the SAME cost,
283	    # so the value follows the stock between warehouses while the net GL effect is nil.
284	    if method == CostingMethod.MOVING_AVERAGE:
285	        cost, _residual = await costing_mav.mav_issue(
286	            session, tenant_id, item.id, from_warehouse_id, qty, currency_code
287	        )
288	        unit_cost = (cost / qty) if qty > 0 else Decimal(0)
289	        await costing_mav.mav_receive(
290	            session, tenant_id, item.id, to_warehouse_id, qty, unit_cost
291	        )
292	    else:
293	        cost = await costing_fifo.consume_layers(
294	            session,
295	            tenant_id,
296	            item_id=item.id,
297	            warehouse_id=from_warehouse_id,
298	            issue_move_id=move.id,
299	            qty=qty,
300	            currency_code=currency_code,
301	        )
302	        unit_cost = (cost / qty) if qty > 0 else Decimal(0)
303	        await costing_fifo.create_layer(
304	            session,
305	            tenant_id,
306	            item_id=item.id,
307	            warehouse_id=to_warehouse_id,
308	            receipt_move_id=move.id,
309	            received_at=move.move_date,
310	            qty=qty,
311	            unit_cost=unit_cost,
312	        )
313	    move.unit_cost = unit_cost
314	    return CostingResult(unit_cost=unit_cost, event=None)
315	
316	
317	async def _current_unit_cost(
318	    session: AsyncSession,
319	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
320	    item: Item,
321	    warehouse_id: uuid.UUID,
322	    method: CostingMethod,
323	) -> Decimal:
324	    """The current per-unit cost of an (item, warehouse) for a value-neutral transfer's ledger
325	    entry:
326	    the moving-average avg, or the FIFO weighted average of the live layers. Reads only (no
327	    writes)."""
328	    if method == CostingMethod.MOVING_AVERAGE:
329	        return await costing_mav.mav_avg_cost(session, tenant_id, item.id, warehouse_id)
330	    return await costing_mav.fifo_weighted_cost(session, tenant_id, item.id, warehouse_id)
331	
332	
333	def _require_entry_cost(move: StockMove) -> Decimal:
334	    """A RECEIPT / positive ADJUSTMENT REQUIRES the entry unit_cost (D-020) — without it the value
335	    entering inventory is undefined. Validated at the service edge (create_move) too; this is the
336	    last guard before the value lands."""
337	    if move.unit_cost is None:
338	        raise ValidationFailedError(
339	            message="A receipt requires a unit cost (the value at which stock enters)",
340	            code="inventory.receipt_unit_cost_required",
341	            details={"move_id": str(move.id)},
342	        )
343	    return Decimal(move.unit_cost)
344	
345	
346	def _build_event(
347	    move: StockMove,
348	    warehouse_id: uuid.UUID,
349	    qty: Decimal,
350	    total_cost: Decimal,
351	    residual_flush: Decimal,
352	    inventory_account_id: uuid.UUID,
353	    offset_account_id: uuid.UUID,
354	    price_diff_account_id: uuid.UUID,
355	    *,
356	    is_inbound: bool,
357	) -> StockValued:
358	    return StockValued(
359	        tenant_id=move.tenant_id,
360	        move_id=move.id,

2	so finance's ``handlers.py`` may import these typed classes (the STRUCTURE §5 events.py allowance,
3	explicitly covering finance importing "upward" from inventory because events carry no behaviour).
4	
5	``StockValued`` is fired inside ``create_move`` AFTER the move + quant + valuation/layer updates,
6	carrying the computed value delta and the THREE GL account ids resolved from the item's category at
7	publish time (D-029 opaque ids). ``finance/handlers.py`` subscribes and posts the COGS/inventory
8	journal in the SAME transaction (D-011/D-020), so the move and its journal commit or roll back as
9	one

11	
12	ONE event for every value-changing move; the handler branches on ``move_type`` for the per-type
13	postings (RECEIPT / ISSUE / ADJUSTMENT up/down). A value-neutral within-warehouse TRANSFER does NOT
14	publish (no value change → no journal). All amounts are full-precision Decimals; the handler
15	quantizes
16	the posted COGS to the currency's decimals (D-015).

32	      same transaction, rolling the whole move back — you cannot move stock into a closed period).

35	      vs decrease) since both carry move_type ADJUSTMENT.

1	"""Finance domain-event handlers (D-011) — the FIRST real cross-module handler (PLAN 5.3, D-020).
2	
3	Subscribes to ``inventory.stock.valued`` and posts the COGS/inventory valuation journal in the SAME
4	transaction as the stock move (D-011 run_in_uow drains before commit; D-020 same-transaction COGS).
5	Because the handler shares the session and any handler exception rolls the WHOLE transaction back, a
6	stock move can never commit without its journal entry, or vice versa — the load-bearing atomicity
7	invariant. The journal posts with the move's ``move_date``: a date in a CLOSED period makes the
8	journal's period trigger fire inside this same transaction, which rolls the whole move back (you
9	cannot move stock into a closed accounting period — correct by construction).
10	
11	Postings per move type (the GL effect of each — D-020). The costing engine pre-selects the OFFSET
12	account per type and the event carries it, so the handler is a thin Dr/Cr direction switch:
13	- RECEIPT / ADJUSTMENT-up: Dr inventory / Cr price-difference. A STANDALONE receipt (opening
14	  balance, manual stock-in) has no procurement GR clearing yet, so its offset is price-difference /
15	  inventory-adjustment account; procurement's goods-receipt path (6.x) will OVERRIDE this with its
16	  own GR/IR offset. ADJUSTMENT-up is the same shape (a stock increase with no document behind it).
17	- ISSUE: Dr COGS / Cr inventory at the computed cost (goods left for sale/production).
18	- ADJUSTMENT-down: Dr price-difference / Cr inventory (an inventory write-off, no document).
19	- The moving-average zero-quantity FLUSH posts its residual to price-difference WITHIN the issue's
20	  entry so value and quantity never disagree (D-020).
21	- A reversal posts the EXACT reverse of the original move's entry (reversing an issue credits COGS;
22	  reversing a receipt debits price-difference) — the costing engine sets the reversal's offset.
23	- TRANSFER within one inventory account: value-neutral → the inventory engine publishes NO event, so
24	  the handler never runs for it (documented; no journal).
25	
26	The journal is built through the finance posting service (``create_draft_entry`` + ``post_entry``),
27	NEVER raw inserts, so every journal invariant (balance, one-side CHECK, period, immutability,
28	numbering, audit, docflow) fires exactly as for any posting. The move's document is linked to the
29	journal entry's document ('posts' edge) so the docflow viewer shows move -> COGS entry.
30	
31	Registration: ``app.main.register_event_handlers`` subscribes ``post_stock_valuation_journal`` to
32	the
33	event key at the app factory (the deterministic D-011 registration seam), so the test harness can
34	re-register after its per-test ``clear_subscriptions`` reset (D-025) without a module re-import.
35	"""
36	
37	from __future__ import annotations
38	
39	import uuid
40	from datetime import date
41	from decimal import Decimal
42	
43	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
44	
45	from app.core import docflow
46	from app.core.money import quantize_for_currency
47	from app.modules.finance import queries as finance_queries
48	from app.modules.finance.constants import DocumentType
49	from app.modules.finance.schemas import JournalEntryCreate, JournalLineCreate
50	from app.modules.finance.service.journal import create_draft_entry, post_entry
51	from app.modules.inventory.constants import DEFAULT_COSTING_CURRENCY, STOCK_MOVE_POSTS_LINK
52	from app.modules.inventory.events import StockValued
53	
54	# A signed posting: (account_id, amount). Positive amount => debit, negative => credit. The line
55	# builder drops zeros and splits into the journal's one-sided debit/credit lines.
56	_SignedPosting = tuple[uuid.UUID, Decimal]
57	
58	
59	async def post_stock_valuation_journal(session: AsyncSession, event: StockValued) -> None:
60	    """Post the COGS/inventory journal for a valued stock move (D-020), in the move's transaction.
61	
62	    Registered via ``app.main.register_event_handlers`` (the deterministic D-011 registration seam),
63	    not an import-time ``@on`` decorator, so the test harness can re-register it after its per-test
64	    ``clear_subscriptions`` reset (D-025) without relying on a module re-import.
65	
66	    Builds the signed postings for the move type, turns them into balanced one-sided journal lines,
67	    posts a COGS-typed entry dated the move date (the period trigger fires here — a closed period
68	    rolls the whole move back), and links move.document -> entry.document ('posts')."""
69	    currency_code = (
70	        await finance_queries.functional_currency_or_none(session, event.tenant_id)
71	        or DEFAULT_COSTING_CURRENCY
72	    )
73	    # total_cost is already quantized for ISSUE (per-layer / MAV quantize) but a RECEIPT's
74	    # qty × unit_cost can carry sub-currency digits — quantize the posted amount at the boundary
75	    # (D-015); the residual flush is already an exact MoneyType difference.
76	    amount = quantize_for_currency(Decimal(event.total_cost), currency_code)
77	    residual = Decimal(event.residual_to_price_difference)
78	
79	    postings = _postings_for(event, amount, residual)
80	    lines = _lines_from_postings(postings, event.item_id)
81	    if len(lines) < 2:
82	        # A zero-value move (e.g. a free receipt) produces no balanced entry — nothing to post. The
83	        # quant/valuation still updated; there is simply no GL effect. (Not reachable on priced
84	        # moves.)
85	        return
86	
87	    entry = await create_draft_entry(
88	        session,
89	        event.tenant_id,
90	        JournalEntryCreate(
91	            posting_date=date.fromisoformat(event.move_date),
92	            currency_code=currency_code,
93	            description=f"Stock {event.move_type.lower()} {event.move_number}",
94	            document_type=DocumentType.COGS,
95	            lines=lines,
96	        ),
97	    )
98	    await post_entry(session, event.tenant_id, entry.id)
99	    # Link the move's document to the journal entry's document so the docflow chain shows the COGS
100	    # posting (D-012 'posts' edge — the finance posting convention).
101	    await docflow.link_documents(
102	        session,
103	        event.tenant_id,
104	        predecessor=event.document_id,
105	        successor=entry.document_id,
106	        link_type=STOCK_MOVE_POSTS_LINK,
107	    )
108	
109	
110	def _postings_for(
111	    event: StockValued, amount: Decimal, residual: Decimal
112	) -> list[_SignedPosting]:
113	    """The signed GL postings (positive = debit, negative = credit) for the move (D-020).
114	
115	    The costing engine already chose ``offset_account_id`` per move type (ISSUE -> COGS; RECEIPT /
116	    ADJUSTMENT -> price-difference; a reversal -> the opposite of the original's offset), so the
117	    handler stays a thin Dr/Cr direction switch:
118	    - inbound: Dr inventory / Cr offset (stock entered or an issue was reversed).
119	    - outbound: Dr offset / Cr inventory (stock left or a receipt was reversed). The inventory leg
120	      additionally carries the moving-average zero-quantity residual, flushed to price-difference,
121	      so value and quantity reconcile to zero (D-020). ``residual`` is 0 unless the issue drove
122	      on-hand to exactly zero."""
123	    if event.is_inbound:
124	        return [
125	            (event.inventory_account_id, amount),
126	            (event.offset_account_id, -amount),
127	        ]
128	    return [
129	        (event.offset_account_id, amount),
130	        (event.inventory_account_id, -(amount + residual)),
131	        (event.price_difference_account_id, residual),
132	    ]
133	
134	
135	def _lines_from_postings(
136	    postings: list[_SignedPosting], item_id: uuid.UUID
137	) -> list[JournalLineCreate]:
138	    """Collapse signed postings per account, drop zeros, and emit one-sided journal lines (D-017):
139	    a positive net is a debit, a negative net a credit. The item dimension rides every line so the
140	    COGS entry is attributable to the item (D-017 dimensions)."""
141	    net: dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal] = {}
142	    for account_id, signed in postings:
143	        net[account_id] = net.get(account_id, Decimal(0)) + signed
144	    lines: list[JournalLineCreate] = []
145	    for account_id, value in net.items():
146	        if value == 0:
147	            continue
148	        if value > 0:
149	            lines.append(
150	                JournalLineCreate(
151	                    account_id=account_id,
152	                    transaction_debit_amount=value,
153	                    item_id=item_id,
154	                )
155	            )
156	        else:
157	            lines.append(
158	                JournalLineCreate(
159	                    account_id=account_id,
160	                    transaction_credit_amount=-value,
161	                    item_id=item_id,
162	                )
163	            )
164	    return lines
165	
166	
167	__all__ = ["post_stock_valuation_journal"]

1	"""Purpose-keyed account wiring (D-019), split out of service/fx.py to keep both under the cap.
2	
3	A ``PostingDefault`` maps a purpose string (e.g. ``'fx_unrealized_gain'``) to a GL account, so any
4	flow that must post to a CONFIGURED account resolves it data-driven rather than hard-coding an
5	account code. The FX engine is the first consumer (gain/loss + revaluation adjustment); AP/AR and
6	inventory COGS reuse the same mechanism in later phases. Kept a distinct concern file (not in
7	fx.py) because it is account wiring, not FX rate math.
8	"""
9	
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	import uuid
13	
14	from sqlalchemy import select
15	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
16	
17	from app.core.exceptions import ValidationFailedError
18	from app.core.pagination import DEFAULT_LIMIT, OrderKey, SortDirection, paginate
19	from app.core.schemas import Page

21	from app.modules.finance.models import Account, PostingDefault
